Performers
Chicago Symphony Orchestra (orchestra), Fritz Reiner (conductor) Documented

Named on the original RCA sleeve. Individual orchestral players are not identified.

[3] [1]
Work version
Orchestral overture Documented

The LP identifies the overture. The particular edition and orchestral parts used in the session are not established. The historical Ricordi score supplies the listening guide’s broad formal divisions, not a claim of bar-by-bar alignment.

[3] [5]
Recorded
1958-11-22 Documented

The dated review of RCA’s reissue gives this session date for the Rossini programme. This is distinct from the 1959 LP publication and the 2021 transfer; a particular session take has not been established.

[4]
Place
Orchestra Hall, Chicago, Illinois, United States Documented

The reissue review names the recording venue.

[4]
Label
RCA Victor Red Seal Documented

Original US mono LP, not a later Living Stereo CD or SACD.

[3] [1]
Catalogue
LM 2318 — Rossini Overtures Documented

The sleeve bears LM-2318 and © RCA 1959; the Internet Archive catalogue dates this issue to 1959.

[3] [1]
Matrix, take, sides
Side 2, band 1 Documented

The sleeve’s running order and the segmented filename agree. The runout matrix, stamper, session take and original tape number are not established.

[3] [2]
Transfer
Internet Archive LP transfer Documented

Attributed to the institution; the source’s operator-account address is not reproduced. The original sleeve separately credits Richard Mohr as musical director and Lewis Layton as recording engineer; those are not digital-transfer credits.

[1]
Transfer date
2021-11-12 Documented

The item’s ripping_date is 20211112022420. Its 27 October 2021 scan date records a different event.

[1]
Processing
Technics SL1200MK5 turntable with Audio-⁠Technica AT95e cartridge → Radio Design Labs EZ-PH1 phono preamp → Focusrite Scarlett 2i2; segmented VBR MP3 access derivative. Documented

The source documents this playback and digitisation chain. Equalisation, pitch correction, noise reduction and any further restoration settings are not established.

[1] [2]
Composition rights
Rossini’s underlying composition is out of copyright under ordinary life-plus-70 terms. Inferred, not documented

Rossini died in 1868. The overture originated in Aureliano in Palmira in 1813 and was reused in Elisabetta in 1815 and Barber in 1816. This assessment does not clear unidentified modern editions.

[7] [6] [5]
Recording rights
Territorial EU public-domain basis: documented commercial publication in 1959, before 1963. Documented

Selected under the project’s eu-published-before-1963 rule. The pre-extension fifty-year term had expired before 1 November 2013. This is not a worldwide public-domain claim, a Creative Commons licence, or a claim that the 1959 recording is out of copyright in the United States.
